sentences.text: 2. Heard the learned counsel for the parties.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that in a full- fledged trial, accused Nos.1 to 3, 5 and 6,
who were tried for the alleged offences on similar allegations have been acquitted by the Trial Court in CC No.1837/2020 vide judgment and order of acquittal dated 08.06.2023.
He submits that the said judgment and order of acquittal has attained finality.
As against the petitioner, split-up case has been registered in CC NC: 2024:KHC:10166 No.826/2023.
Continuation of the proceedings in the said case is a futile exercise and accordingly, he prays to allow the petition.

4. Per contra, learned HCGP submits that petitioner had not appeared before the Trial Court and therefore, split-up case has been registered against him and NBW is also issued against him.
However, he does not dispute the fact that the judgment and order of acquittal passed by the Trial Court as against other accused persons who were tried for similar offences, has attained finality.

5. FIR in Crime No.44/2018 was registered by Women Police Station, Dakshina Kannada District,
Mangaluru on the complaint of Smt. Farheen Sheikh, against six persons.

entities.text: Women Police Station, Dakshina Kannada District
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Petitioner was arraigned as accused No.4 in the FIR.
After completion of investigation, charge sheet was filed as against six accused and petitioner was arraigned as accused No.4 even in the charge sheet.
Since the petitioner did not appear before the Trial Court, a split-up case was registered against him in CC No.826/2023.

Insofar as other accused are concerned, namely, accused Nos.1 to 3, 5 and 6, who were tried for the alleged NC: 2024:KHC:10166 offences by the Trial Court in CC No.1837/2023 vide judgment and order dated 08.06.2023 they have been acquitted and the said judgment and order of acquittal has Mohammed Althaf vs The State Of Karnataka on 12 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119623173/
2 attained finality.

entities.text: Mohammed Althaf vs The State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The charges against all the accused persons in the case are similar.

6. A perusal of the judgment and order of acquittal passed in CC No.1837/2023 would go to show that material witnesses have turned hostile and therefore, the learned Trial Judge had refused the request of the learned public prosecutor to examine the remaining charge sheet witnesses and has thereafter passed the judgment and order of acquittal acquitting accused Nos.1 to 3, 5 and 6.

Under the circumstances, continuation of the impugned proceedings in CC No.826/2023 as against the petitioner herein, who is the elder brother of accused No.1, husband of de-facto complainant, would be a futile exercise and waste of court's time.
Under the circumstances, I am of the opinion that the prayer made by the petitioner in this petition requires to be granted.

Accordingly, the following order:-
7. The Criminal Petition is allowed.

The entire proceedings in CC No.826/2023 pending before the Court of JMFC III, Mangaluru, arising out of Crime No.44/2018 registered by NC: 2024:KHC:10166 Women Police Station, Dakshina Kannada, Mangaluru, for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 506 read with Section 34 of IPC and Section 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, is quashed.
